metadata.title: Carson Wentz - Cleared for backup role
metadata.description: Wentz (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game at Green Bay, but Kirk Cousins will be Minnesota's starting quarterback.
metadata.analysis: Kyler Murray (hamstring) is out for another week but may eventually replace Wentz as the No. 2 quarterback. Wentz's miserable performance against the Bills last week likely was a factor in the Vikings trading for Cousins.

metadata.title: Carson Wentz (ankle) off injury report Sunday
metadata.description: Carson Wentz is off the injury report for Sunday's game against the Packers.
metadata.analysis: Wentz will backup Kirk Cousins on Sunday.

metadata.title: Carson Wentz (ankle) limited in practice Thursday
metadata.description: Carson Wentz was limited in practice on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Wentz will figure to backup Kirk Cousins on Sunday against the Packers.

metadata.title: Carson Wentz - Limited again Thursday
metadata.description: Wentz (ankle) practiced in a limited capacity Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Wentz had his left ankle stepped on by Vikings left guard Joe Huber during Monday's loss to the Bills, and while he didn't miss a snap before Max Brosmer took over for the final possession, the former has operated with practice restrictions to begin Week 10 prep. With the acquisition of Kirk Cousins on Tuesday and Kyler Murray still week to week due to a Grade 2 hamstring strain, Wentz is expected to return to a reserve role Sunday at Green Bay, but head coach Kevin O'Connell hasn't announced a starter for that contest as of Thursday.

metadata.title: Carson Wentz - Listed as limited
metadata.description: Wentz (ankle) is listed as limited on Wednesday's estimated practice report, Ben Goessling of The Minnesota Star Tribune reports.
metadata.analysis: Wentz injured his ankle Monday night during his disastrous start against the Bills. The Vikings have since traded for Kirk Cousins, who likely will take over as the starter for Sunday's game at Green Bay. Coach Kevin O'Connell wouldn't commit to starting Cousins and suggested Kyler Murray (hamstring) is unlikely to play, but Cousins' familiarity with the scheme and terminology means he shouldn't need long to prepare.

metadata.title: Carson Wentz absolutely awful in Monday night loss
metadata.description: Carson Wentz completed only 8-of-25 passes for 81 yards with no touchdowns and two interceptions in Monday's 23-6 loss to the Bills.
metadata.analysis: Earlier this season, Wentz had some bright moments at the helm of the Vikings' offense. That's a distant memory now, as the veteran QB couldn't even finish Monday's contest without being benched in favor of third-stringer Max Brosmer. Wentz may have very well played his final snaps for the Vikings.

metadata.title: Vikings in QB Market after Carson Wentz Struggles
metadata.description: According to Mike Garafolo of the NFL Network, the Minnesota Vikings will be looking to acquire a quarterback via trade before Tuesday's NFL Trade Deadline. Carson Wentz completed only eight of his 25 pass attempts on Monday Night Football against the Bills, totaling only 81 passing yards and throwing a pair of interceptions. The Vikings were held to two field goals in their 23-6 home loss. Minnesota's defense has been elite this year, and they have a strong group of pass-catchers led by Justin Jefferson. However, the offense has been held back by mediocre QB play from Wentz and Kyler Murray (hamstring). Murray is dealing with a Grade 2 hamstring strain and could miss multiple games, and if a new QB came in and played well, he could earn the starting role for the rest of the season. Some of the potentially available options include Daniel Jones of the Colts and Kirk Cousins of the Raiders, who each have some history with the team and current coaching staff.

metadata.title: Carson Wentz - Forgettable performance in spot start
metadata.description: Wentz completed eight of 25 passes for 81 yards with no touchdowns and two interceptions and rushed once for no gain in the Vikings' 23-6 loss to the Bills on Monday night. He also lost a fumble.
metadata.analysis: Wentz had typically put together competent performances in his opportunities to lead head coach Kevin O'Connell's offense in the past, but Monday night was a clear exception. Wentz only took one sack, but he banged up his right hand on a first-half pass attempt, then had his foot stepped on by offensive lineman Joe Huber in the second half, the latter which required a visit to the medical tent. Wentz also repeatedly failed to master what had been a vulnerable Bills pass defense, averaging a minuscule 3.2 yards per attempt. Wentz tossed interceptions on back-to-back drives to open the second half as well, and although they only led to one field goal for Buffalo, they were indicative of the kind of night it was for the veteran signal-caller. Wentz was ultimately pulled for Max Brosmer for the Vikings' final drive, and if Murray can't suit up for a Week 10 road showdown with the Packers on Sunday, it remains to be seen if Wentz will get another crack at a starting assignment.

metadata.title: Carson Wentz Implodes in Plus Matchup
metadata.description: Minnesota Vikings quarterback Carson Wentz completed eight of 25 passes for 81 yards, no touchdowns, and two interceptions in his team's 23-6 loss to the visiting Buffalo Bills. He gained no yards on his sole rush and was also credited with a fumble lost. Wentz got the starting nod in relief of teammate Kyler Murray (hamstring), who was unable to go after a week of DNPs. The veteran was flat-out abysmal in this one, unable to orchestrate a single touchdown drive. Wentz was eventually benched for Max Brosmer late in the fourth quarter, though it's worth mentioning that the former did get checked out for an injury in the blue medical tent at one point. Either way, it was a forgettable performance that hurt the offense's output. This could be Wentz's last start, depending on Murray's status moving forward. Still, it's fair to wonder whether he'd be benched in favor of Brosmer after the dreadful outing anyway. Minnesota is slated for a road matchup with the Green Bay Packers next Sunday.

metadata.title: Bills Defense Tasked With Stopping Carson Wentz
metadata.description: The Bills' defense is RotoBaller's 11th-ranked unit entering Week 9, when Buffalo will meet up with the Minnesota Vikings. Minnesota will send Carson Wentz onto the field for his second start of the season, as starting quarterback Kyler Murray is out with a hamstring injury. Wentz helped lead the Vikings to a Week 2 win over the Chicago Bears, completing just 11 of 20 passes for 143 yards, while he was held without a touchdown during the 9-3 victory. The Bills' defense is projected to score eight fantasy points against Minnesota on Monday night. Buffalo is coming off its best defensive effort of the season during a 36-10 win over the Baltimore Ravens last week. Buffalo limited Baltimore to just 144 total yards during the Week 8 triumph.

metadata.title: Carson Wentz Has Potential In Week 9, And Possibly Beyond
metadata.description: With quarterback Kyler Murray (hamstring) set to miss Week 9, Minnesota Vikings backup Carson Wentz carries potential for a Monday night game against Buffalo. The veteran has his flaws -- he took 19 sacks in five starts last year -- but he also can provide the downfield spark this offense so desperately needs against a Bills defense that ranks 22nd against fantasy quarterbacks. Wentz's three-touchdown performance in relief in Week 1 remains the Vikings' best passing game of the year, and at minimum, he will give top receiver Justin Jefferson plenty of chances. Even in one-QB formats, the journeyman is worth a speculative stash for managers looking to solidify their bench or repair their roster after a QB injury. The Vikings may still trade for another quarterback, but if Wentz plays well, he'll have the inside track to continue starting. As RotoBaller's No. 20 QB this week, Wentz is starting caliber in Superflex leagues, but there's also a chance he could carry value beyond this week if the Vikings look good on Monday.

metadata.title: Carson Wentz will start in Week 9 for Vikings
metadata.description: Carson Wentz will start Monday's game against the Bills.
metadata.analysis: Kyler Murray is continuing to battle a sore hamstring. Wentz will be a QB2 for fantasy managers in 2-QB and superflex leagues.

metadata.title: Carson Wentz - In line to draw MNF start
metadata.description: Wentz is stated to start Monday night's game against the Bills, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
metadata.analysis: Wentz will get the Week 9 assignment at QB for the Vikings, with Kyler Murray viewed as week-to-week with a hamstring strain, per Ian Rapoport of NFL Network. Max Brosmer will be the team's backup versus Buffalo, and perhaps longer than that should Murray's injury linger. Wentz thus represents an option for those in Superflex formats or otherwise are in need of signal-caller help due to injury or bye week issues.

metadata.title: Carson Wentz trending towards starting in Week 9
metadata.description: Carson Wentz is reportedly trending towards starting in Monday's game against the Bills.
metadata.analysis: Kyler Murray is continuing to be evaluated for his hamstring injury. "His status for Monday night is, at best, up in the air, and it sounds like it is trending toward Carson Wentz starting on Monday night," Adam Schefter said.

metadata.title: Carson Wentz to Start Monday vs. Bills
metadata.description: Minnesota Vikings quarterback Carson Wentz will get the start under center for Monday night's primetime matchup with the Bills, according to NFL Insider Ian Rapoport. Starting quarterback Kyler Murray, who has completed less than 60% of his passes in back-to-back weeks and has thrown only five touchdowns across his six starts, is dealing with what the team has called a "sore hamstring". Wentz has appeared in two 2026 contests, throwing for 133 yards and three touchdowns in relief of Murray in Week 1 before leading the Vikings to victory over the Bears despite throwing for only 143 yards and zero touchdowns in Week 2. Four-time All-Pro wide receiver Justin Jefferson, who currently ranks as the fantasy WR24, had by far his most productive outing of the season in that Week 1 pairing with Wentz, recording season-highs of eight receptions, 92 yards, and two scores.

metadata.title: Carson Wentz Trending Toward Starting in Week 9 Against Bills
metadata.description: ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that the Minnesota Vikings could be trending toward starting Carson Wentz over the injured Kyler Murray (hamstring) for the team's Week 9 Monday clash against Buffalo. Wentz played in two games early in the season after Murray suffered a concussion. He was 12 of 19 passing for 133 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions against Green Bay, then finished 11 of 20 passing for 143 yards, with no TDs or INTs against Chicago. The matchup against Buffalo is a pretty favorable fantasy test, and Minnesota has enough offensive playmakers around to make any QB a viable fantasy option. Wentz has delivered enough over his career to trust him more than the typical backup as well. Murray is the only Minnesota QB in our RotoBaller Week 9 projections right now, sitting at QB16. Wentz will be a better deep-league starting option, despite the favorable matchup ahead.

metadata.title: Carson Wentz - Returning to backup role
metadata.description: Wentz will serve as the Vikings' backup quarterback Sunday against the Buccaneers after head coach Kevin O'Connell announced Monday that Kyler Murray has cleared concussion protocol and will start Week 3.
metadata.analysis: Wentz performed admirably across nearly two full games in relief of Murray, who sustained the concussion midway through the first quarter of the season opener against the Packers. After completing 12 of 19 passes for 133 yards and three touchdowns in the Vikings' come-from-behind 39-22 win over Green Bay, Wentz started Week 2 against the Bears and played turnover-free football in rainy and windy conditions en route to leading Minnesota to a 9-3 win. While Murray will reclaim the starting job now that he's out of the protocol, Wentz's performance over the past two weeks firmly solidifies him ahead of 2024 first-round pick J.J. McCarthy on the depth chart.

metadata.title: Carson Wentz quiet in Week 2 win over Bears
metadata.description: Carson Wentz completed 11-of-20 pass attempts for 143 yards while also rushing three times for six yards in the Vikings' 9-3 Week 2 win over the Chicago Bears.
metadata.analysis: Wentz has struggled to make an impact behind center to begin the season, finishing with less than 145 passing yards in each of the first two games. The quarterback could be relegated to the bench if No. 1 signal-caller Kyler Murray (concussion) is able to suit up for a Week 3 contest against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

metadata.title: Carson Wentz - Can't overcome weather in Chicago
metadata.description: Wentz completed 11 of 20 passes for 143 yards in Sunday's 9-3 win over the Bears. He added six yards on three carries.
metadata.analysis: Neither team reached 200 passing yards on a wet and windy day at Soldier Field, so Wentz had no real opportunity to build on his impressive performance last week in relief of Kyler Murray (concussion), when he threw three TDs. Murray could clear the concussion protocol in time to re-take the reins of the offense in Week 3, returning Wentz to the bench for a road trip to Tampa Bay after he led the Vikings to a 2-0 start to the season.

metadata.title: Carson Wentz Unremarkable As Bad Weather Impacts Game
metadata.description: Minnesota Vikings quarterback Carson Wentz went into game-manager mode during terrible weather conditions on Sunday in Chicago, completing 11 of 20 passes for 143 yards without a touchdown or a turnover in his team's 9-3 win. The veteran backup made a pair of key throws for first downs on Minnesota's last drive, though the Vikings favored the run on a day when neither side scored a touchdown. It was an underwhelming set of circumstances for fantasy managers who started Wentz this week, but he ultimately helped the Vikings win a second straight game to start the season. He's likely headed back to the sideline, as starter Kyler Murray (concussion) is reportedly on track to be ready for Week 3 at Tampa Bay.

metadata.title: Carson Wentz - Will start Sunday at Chicago
metadata.description: Coach Kevin O'Connell said Friday that Wentz will be the Vikings' starting quarterback Sunday at Chicago with Kyler Murray (concussion) ruled out for that contest.
metadata.analysis: Wentz stepped in for Murray 12 plays into this past Sunday's game against the Packers and helped guide the Vikings to a 39-22 win, but the former completed 12 of 19 passes for just 133 yards. Wentz did toss three touchdowns -- 39 and nine yards to Justin Jefferson, 16 yards to T.J. Hockenson -- but otherwise he managed the game and didn't commit a turnover. O'Connell relayed to Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com that he expects Murray to clear the concussion protocol next week, so Sunday's nod could be Wentz's last for some time.

metadata.title: Carson Wentz set to start for Week 2
metadata.description: Carson Wentz is set to be Minnesota's starting quarterback in their matchup against the Chicago Bears in Week 2.
metadata.analysis: The Vikings have ruled out Kyler Murray (concussion) ahead of Sunday's game and announced that Wentz would be the starter in his absence. That's good news for the fantasy outlook of Justin Jefferson and Aaron Jones Sr. this week, as Minnesota's offense has been able to produce ample fantasy points in the few occasions that Wentz has been at the helm for the team.

metadata.title: Carson Wentz In Superflex Territory Against Bears
metadata.description: Minnesota Vikings quarterback Carson Wentz is a playable option with a favorable matchup Sunday at Chicago now that Minnesota has ruled out starter Kyler Murray (concussion) from returning in Week 2. The veteran backup played well in relief last week against Green Bay, recovering from a few poor throws early to connect on three touchdowns as the Vikings rallied to beat Green Bay. Now, Wentz will face a Bears defense that ranks 29th in air yards allowed and surrendered 156 yards after the catch last week. The journeyman naturally comes with the risk of turnovers and the inability to avoid sacks that have plagued him most of his career, but he's still facing a shaky defense and throwing to a corps of pass catchers led by receiver Justin Jefferson. As one of RotoBaller's top 24 QB options this week, Wentz is startable in formats that play more than one quarterback.

metadata.title: Carson Wentz to Start Against Bears in Week 2
metadata.description: Minnesota Vikings quarterback Carson Wentz will make his first start of the 2026 season in the Week 2 divisional clash on the road in Chicago against the Bears after head coach Kevin O'Connell announced on Friday that Kyler Murray (concussion) has been ruled out, according to Matthew Coller. The 33-year-old Wentz was forced into the Week 1 contest against the division-rival Green Bay Packers early after Murray suffered a scary concussion, and he proceeded to go 12-for-19 passing for 133 yards, three touchdowns, and zero interceptions in the 39-22 victory. Wentz had a solid day and will now be in a position as a QB2 streamer in deep superflex leagues as the Vikings face off against a Bears defense that allowed nearly 40 points to the Carolina Panthers in the season opener last weekend. Former first-rounder J.J. McCarthy, who lost the starting competition to Murray in training camp, will back Wentz up this weekend. Unfortunately for those who picked up Wentz off waivers this week, Week 2 could be his only start if Murray returns in Week 3 and stays healthy after that.

metadata.title: Carson Wentz - Will likely start in Murray absence
metadata.description: Wentz "is likely to start" Sunday against the Bears if Kyler Murray does not clear concussion protocol, Dan Graziano of ESPN.com reports.
metadata.analysis: Wentz was named the backup quarterback last week and led the Vikings to a Week 1 comeback victory over the Packers, so although fellow reserve J.J. McCarthy would also be an option, Wentz appears to be the favorite to get the nod should Murray be unable to go.

metadata.title: Carson Wentz Likely to Start if Teammate Isn't Cleared
metadata.description: ESPN's Dan Graziano believes that Minnesota Vikings quarterback Carson Wentz is likely to start in Week 2 against the division-rival Chicago Bears if Kyler Murray (concussion) is not cleared in time. Former first-rounder J.J. McCarthy is the one who was competing with Murray for the starting job in training camp, but it is more about the Vikings believing that Wentz's veteran experience will put them in a better position with limited preparation time. Graziano foresees a scenario where Wentz starts this week with McCarthy as the backup, assuming Murray does not clear the league's concussion protocol before Sunday. If Wentz makes the start, he is set up for success. The 33-year-old veteran led the Vikings to a come-from-behind victory over the division-rival Green Bay Packers in Week 1, throwing for 133 yards and three touchdowns, and the Bears just allowed 361 passing yards to Panthers QB Bryce Young. Murray should not be out long-term, but in deep two-QB fantasy leagues, Wentz could be an attractive streamer in Week 2.
